See also: Babysitter, baby-sitter, and baby sitter

English

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • baby-sitter
  • baby sitter (rare)

Etymology

[edit]

From baby +‎ sitter.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Received Pronunciation) IPA(key): /ˈbeɪ̯biˌsɪtə/, [ˈbe̞ɪ̯bɪi̯ˌsɪtʰə]
  • (General American) IPA(key): /ˈbeɪ̯biˌsɪtɚ/, [ˈbeɪ̯bɪi̯ˌsɪɾɚ]
    • Audio (US):(file)
  • (General Australian) IPA(key): /ˈbæ̝ɪ̯biˌsɪtɚ/, [ˈbæ̝ɪ̯bɪi̯ˌsɪɾɚ]
  • Hyphenation: ba‧by‧sit‧ter

Noun

[edit]

babysitter (plural babysitters)

  1. A person who cares for one or more babies or children for a short period of time in place of their legal guardians.
    Synonyms: childsitter, sitter
    Hypernym: childminder
    My neighbor is sometimes a babysitter for other mothers’ children.
  2. (derogatory) A person who has to watch or attend to anything or anyone unnecessarily closely; a coddler or handholder.
    • 2005, Alan Ball, Playing Extra Time, page 158:
      He said he did not want to be on tenterhooks worrying about us and having to act as a babysitter for grown men.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • babysit (via back-formation)
  • babysitter test
  • electronic babysitter

Related terms

[edit]
  • birdsitter
  • catsitter
  • dogsitter
  • homesitter
  • house-sitter
  • petsitter
  • puppysitter
